segments.text: I enjoy cooking when I'm feeding other people, but usually after a busy day at work, I don't enjoy cooking for myself.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well, we're talking about cooking today, and most of us can at least boil an egg, but not everyone could make it as a professional chef in a world-famous restaurant.

segments.speaker: Becca
segments.text: Being a top chef requires passion, dedication and hard work.

segments.text: So why do they do it?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: who started her own award-winning restaurant

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: in the country known as the Home of Fine Dining, France.

segments.text: As usual, we'll be learning some useful new words and phrases.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And remember, you'll find all this episode's vocabulary,

segments.text: But first, I have a question for you now.

segments.text: The top prize for any professional chef are Michelin stars,

segments.text: Born in South Africa, chef Chantelle D'Artagnol started her culinary career at a three Michelin

segments.speaker: Becca
segments.text: star restaurant in the exclusive Mayfair area of London. Here she tells Ruth Alexander,

segments.speaker: Becca
segments.text: presenter of BBC World Service programme The Food Chain, how it all got started.

segments.speaker: Chantel Dartnall
segments.text: What happened is I had graduated from the Prud'Leath College of Food and Wine

segments.speaker: Chantel Dartnall
segments.text: and decided to send my CV to all the three Michelin star restaurants

segments.speaker: Chantel Dartnall
segments.text: that I could find at that moment in the Michelin Guide.

segments.speaker: Ruth Alexander
segments.text: So you aimed high from the off.

segments.speaker: Chantel Dartnall
segments.text: I aimed high. The only thing that they could say was no. And what would I lose?

segments.speaker: Chantel Dartnall
segments.text: I received a call from Chef Paul Rhodes to say, when can you start?

segments.speaker: Ruth Alexander
segments.text: Wow.

segments.speaker: Chantel Dartnall
segments.text: And this sort of just catapulted my career.

segments.speaker: Becca
segments.text: Chantelle sent her CV to the world's top restaurants.

segments.speaker: Becca
segments.text: CV is short for Curriculum Vitae, a document listing someone's education, qualifications and work experience, which they write when looking for a job.

segments.speaker: Becca
segments.text: In American English, it's called a resume.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Chantal applied to only Michelin-starred winning restaurants.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: She aimed high, meaning she was ambitious.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Chantal says the worst they could do is say no,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: a phrase which means you shouldn be afraid of trying to do something because the worst outcome is being rejected

segments.speaker: Becca
segments.text: Luckily for Chantal the answer was yes and learning her trade in a top London restaurant catapulted

segments.speaker: Becca
segments.text: meaning accelerated, her career.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: At the age of 26, Chantal left London and returned home

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: to open her own restaurant, Mosaic, near Pretoria in South Africa.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: She'd been inspired by botanical cuisine,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: the use of edible flowers and herbs to decorate and flavour food.

segments.text: When I opened Mosaic in South Africa,

segments.text: I knew I wanted something entirely different

segments.speaker: Chantel Dartnall
segments.text: and something which diners had not seen.

segments.speaker: Chantel Dartnall
segments.text: I wanted to have my own signature and to stand out.

segments.text: And I think especially for botanical cuisine in South Africa,

segments.speaker: Chantel Dartnall
segments.text: it was very much unknown.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Chantal developed her own signature.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: A signature item is something that is typical of

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: or strongly associated with a particular person or place.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: For example, whiskey is Scotland's signature drink.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Chantal's signature is cooking botanical food.

segments.speaker: Becca
segments.text: Chantal's Mosaic Restaurant is currently at the Chateau de Tenier in northern France,

segments.text: where it's listed among the top 200 restaurants in the world.

segments.speaker: Becca
segments.text: And in 2017, she won the title Best Female Chef in the World.

segments.speaker: Becca
segments.text: These achievements have helped Chantal stand out,

segments.speaker: Becca
segments.text: to be more noticeable and better than other chefs.

segments.text: Chantal is still waiting but surely it only a matter of time until she wins those coveted Michelin stars Speaking of which what was the answer to your question Becca

segments.text: Ah yes, I asked you earlier, who is the winner of the most Michelin stars ever?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I said that it was the Italian chef Enrico Bartolini.

segments.text: But unfortunately, it was incorrect.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Ah, no.

segments.text: The right answer is B, Joël Rubachon, our French chef with 31 stars, the most decorated chef in history.

segments.text: OK, let's recap the vocabulary we've learnt, starting with curriculum vitae, CV or resume in American English,

segments.text: The phrase, the worst they can do is say no, means don't be afraid of trying to do something for the fear of rejection.
